name: Pause Info Card
description: Pause playback and the film or series logo, the episode title and the synopsis fade in over the frame. Plus optional CSS hooks: row names, scroll position and card metadata.
overview: Netflix-style pause info card for the Jellyfin web client

versions.changelog:
**1.2.3.0**

- The pause glyph follows the [Abyss](https://github.com/AumGupta/abyss-jellyfin) accent when that theme is installed. The rest of the card stays white on a black scrim, because it sits over video and that is not a theme decision.

**1.2.2.0**

- A plugin icon, shown in the Jellyfin plugin list.

**1.2.0.0**

- Carries only its own modules now (the pause card and the three CSS hooks) instead of the whole
  bundle, so it can be installed alongside **Episode Picker** without the two fighting over the
  shared framework.
- Its settings are merged into the add-on's global configuration rather than assigned over it, for
  the same reason.

**1.1.0.0**

- Renamed from "JellyFlix Add-on" to **Pause Info Card**. JellyFlix is the repository, which now holds more than one plugin; the plugin is named after what it does. The API routes moved with it: `/PauseInfoCard/addon.js` and `/PauseInfoCard/status`.
- Same plugin GUID, so this is an in-place update and settings are kept.

**1.0.4.0**

- Support clients that play outside the DOM. Jellyfin Desktop / Media Player 1.11+ runs this web client but hands playback to libmpv, so no `<video>` element is ever created and the add-on never saw a pause. State now falls back to the OSD itself.
- With no media duration to measure, the resolved item is validated against the title the OSD is showing instead.

**1.0.3.0**

- Drop `If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since` for the index.html request; a 304 was handing browsers their pre-install copy of the page forever.
- The injected document is sent `no-store`, without ETag or Last-Modified.

**1.0.2.0**

- Ask for index.html uncompressed. Jellyfin gzips it for anything that sends `Accept-Encoding`, i.e. every browser.

**1.0.1.0**

- Intercept through `IHttpResponseBodyFeature`; never rewrite a compressed or non-HTML response. New status endpoint.

**1.0.0.0** — first release.

**1.1.1.0**

- Follows the [Abyss](https://github.com/AumGupta/abyss-jellyfin) palette when it is installed: accent, glass tint, corner radius and easing all come from its `--abyss-*` variables, with this stylesheet's own values as fallbacks. The frosted backdrop is applied only when Abyss defines the blur, so it costs nothing on a TV otherwise.

**1.1.0.0**

- Usable with a TV remote: focus lands on the episode you are watching, Up/Down walks the list, Left/Right changes season instead of seeking, Enter starts the episode, Back closes.

**1.0.4.0**

- Input no longer leaks through the drawer into the player (play/pause on `pointerdown`, volume on the wheel).
- A plugin icon, shown in the Jellyfin plugin list.

**1.0.0.0** — first release.

name: Episode Picker
description: Adds a button to the player while a series is playing. It opens a drawer with the episodes of the current season — thumbnails, how far through each one you are, the one you are watching marked — and a season selector. Picking an episode starts it.
overview: Netflix-style episode and season picker inside the player

versions.changelog:
**1.0.0.0** — first release.

- Films and series: Polish title, original title, synopsis, genres, production countries, premiere
  date, the users' rating as the community rating and the critics' as the critic rating.
- Directors and cast with photos. Filmweb does not publish character names, so actors come without
  their roles.
- The Polish poster, and stills offered as backdrops.
- A **Filmweb** field in the Identify dialog that takes an id or a pasted page address, and a link
  to the title's page among the item's external links.

name: Filmweb
description: Search Filmweb.pl from the Identify dialog and fill films and series from it: Polish title and synopsis, genres, production countries, premiere date, the users' and the critics' rating, directors and cast with photos, the Polish poster and stills. Uses the unofficial REST API of the Filmweb website.
overview: Filmweb.pl as a metadata source for films and series
